summary: The baseline remains far from underwriting-complete: runtime contains only one publishable methodology-1.0 score record (GEV), so 249 active-universe companies still require sourced comparable underwriting before T0. The targeted XTND capital-structure directive advanced materially from primary SEC evidence: the September 4 S-8 registers 43,567,442 shares across rollover awards, the 2026 incentive plan and ESPP, while the September 3 pro forma shows a 277,442,600 basic/diluted pro forma weighted-average denominator, $32.3M six-month pro forma revenue, $34.5M operating loss, and preliminary merger accounting. Exact post-close common/pre-funded-warrant capitalization and normalized cash-flow runway remain unresolved, so XTND must not be admitted/scored on this evidence alone.

materialFindings.finding: T0 underwriting breadth is incomplete: score-state currently contains only GEV while system-state reports scoredCompanies=1 and publishableCompanies=1 out of 250.

XTND filed Form S-8 on 2026-09-04 registering 9,936,483 rollover-award shares, 18,630,959 shares under the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan, and 15,000,000 shares under the 2026 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, totaling 43,567,442 registered plan/rollover shares. This is material potential equity overhang and must be normalized against post-close outstanding shares rather than treated as immediate dilution.

XTND's merger pro forma reports 277,442,600 weighted-average shares basic and diluted for both the six months ended 2026-06-30 and FY2025 pro forma periods. The filing also reports six-month pro forma revenue of $32.333M, gross profit $3.207M, operating loss $34.465M and net loss $27.545M, highlighting substantial current operating-loss intensity relative to revenue.

The pro forma states merger accounting/purchase-price allocations remain preliminary and may differ materially after final valuation; it also shows the minimum-cash condition depended on a $60M contribution tied to warrant exercises. These facts prevent treating the pro forma denominator or liquidity presentation as a final normalized post-close capitalization/runway view.

The S-8 confirms the merger closed September 3, 2026 and details conversion/cash exercise/cashless exercise mechanics for legacy JFB securities and rollover awards, creating multiple share-issuance pathways that must be reconciled before any fully diluted per-share valuation.
